rules.sentence: The syndrome is primarily identified by ECG findings of right bundle branch block and distinct ST-segment changes in the right precordial leads (V1-V3).

Type 1 is defined by coved ST-segment elevation of at least 2 mm in at least 1 right precordial lead, followed by T-wave inversions, in the absence of other causes of ST elevation (see Image. Brugada Syndrome Type 1 Morphology).
Type 2 presents as saddleback-shaped ST-segment elevation of at least 2 mm, with a positive or biphasic T wave and J-point elevation of at least 1 mm.
Type 3 is characterized by ST-segment elevation less than 1 mm with a positively deflecting T wave (see Image. Brugada Syndrome Electrocardiographic Patterns).
